newsitem.title: USA: ADM needs more board changes -- union.
newsitem.headline: ADM needs more board changes -- union.

text.p: The United Brotherhood of Carpenters said Friday the reorganization of the top management at Archer Daniels Midland Co is not enough to satisfy its demands for sweeping change at the company.
"It's fair to say that this isn't the dramatic reform that's necessary in the leadership ranks at ADM," Ed Durkin, director of special programs at the union, said in a statement.
The carpenters union, which holds about 770,000 ADM shares, has been pressing for changes in ADM's management and board of directors.

On Thursday, ADM announced the formation of a four-member office of the chief executive, including Chairman Dwayne Andreas, President James Randall, Charles Bayless, who is president of ADM's processing division, and G. Allen Andreas, who is counsel to the executive committee of the board of directors.

"As long as Mr. Andreas holds the position of chairman and chief executive, very little is likely to change in terms of how the business is run," Durkin said. "Until the company's board is transformed into a truly independent body, meaningful reform will be slow in coming."
The union's call for reform follows ADM's guilty pleas to two counts of price fixing and an agreement to pay $100 million in fines as part of a U.S. Justice Department probe.
Earlier Friday, the California Public Employees' Retirement Systems (CalPERS) said it was skeptical about management changes at ADM since no outside individuals were named to top offices.
